case_name: Balak Ram and another v State Of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State Of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

16 August 1974
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION : Criminal Appeal No. 72 of 1973. Appeal by Special leave from the Judgment and Order dated the 22nd December 1972 of the Allahabad High Court in Crl. A. No. 895 of 1972 and Referred No. 82 of 1972 and Criminal Appeal Nos. 25, 34-35 of 1973
The Judgment was delivered by : Y. V. Chandrachud, J.
1. On May 27, 1971 two persons called Tribeni Sahai and Radhey were shot dead in the town of Dataganj, District Budaun. The four appellants : Balak Ram, Nathoo, Dr. R. P. Kohli and Mohd. Sayeed Khan @ Banney Khan were tried along with two
facts: May 27, 1971: Two persons called Tribeni Sahai and Radhey were shot dead in Dataganj, District Budaun.
Four appellants: Balak Ram, Nathoo, Dr. R. P. Kohli, and Mohd. Sayeed Khan @ Banney Khan were tried for various offences in connection with the incident.
Balak Ram was convicted u/s. 302 of the Penal Code and was sentenced to death.
The High Court confirmed the conviction of Balak Ram and the sentence of death imposed on him u/s. 302 as also his conviction u/s. 148.

In an appeal against the order of acquittal passed by the Sessions Court, the High Court confirmed the acquittal of Kailash, but convicted Nathoo, Dr. R. P. Kohli, and Mohd. Sayeed Khan @ Banney Khan u/s.s 302 and 307 read with s. 149.

The three accused have been sentenced by the High Court to imprisonment for life for their participation in the murder of Tribeni Sahai and Radhey and concurrently to ten years' rigorous imprisonment for causing injuries to Jhilmili and Ram Prakash.
issues: Whether the appellants were guilty of the offences charged against them.
Whether the evidence was sufficient to prove the guilt of the appellants beyond reasonable doubt.
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution failed to establish a prima facie case against the appellants.
The evidence was circumstantial and did not prove the guilt of the appellants beyond reasonable doubt.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution had established a strong prima facie case against the appellants.
The evidence was sufficient to prove the guilt of the appellants beyond reasonable doubt.
court_reasoning: The court found that the prosecution had established a strong prima facie case against the appellants and that the evidence was sufficient to prove their guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
The court rejected the appellants' arguments that the prosecution failed to establish a prima facie case against them.
holding: The conviction of Balak Ram, Nathoo, Dr. R. P. Kohli, and Mohd. Sayeed Khan @ Banney Khan was upheld by the High Court.
The sentence of death imposed on Balak Ram was confirmed by the High Court.
